key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power, welding speed, and current govern molten pool flow, weld geometry, and arc stability.
engineering_relevance: These trends can guide parameter selection for welding low-expansion Invar components used in aerospace composite molds.
method: Numerical simulation of molten pool dynamics
Parameter analysis: 5–6 kW laser power, 0.5–0.8 m/min speed, and 150–170 A current
evidence_signal: Within the studied ranges, higher power increased penetration and keyhole size, higher speed reduced penetration and weld width, and higher current widened the weld and stabilized the arc.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative validation errors or joint-property tests, so these parameter trends do not establish a production-ready welding window.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
